title: The Rise of AI in Weather and Climate Information and its Impact on Global Inequality

bias_targets.methodology: Analyzing the spatial distribution of observational training data (e.g., weather stations, flux towers) and evaluating spatial disparities in model loss functions and predictive performance between data-dense (Global North) and data-sparse (Global South) regions.

Reviewing disparities in predictive forecast accuracy (e.g., comparing weather forecast skill improvements in high-income versus low-income countries) and assessing the unequal global distribution of computational infrastructure (HPC) required for AI model development.

Evaluating the source corpora of climate-specific Large Language Models (LLMs) for the overrepresentation of Western hegemonic viewpoints, languages, and scientific literature, which propagates structural biases in climate knowledge synthesis.
